title: Back up and erase | mac.riera.co.uk
summary: How to back up an Apple silicon Mac with Time Machine, check the backup, and erase it with Erase All Content and Settings on macOS 26.
body: Back up and erase a Mac Make a fresh Time Machine backup Export what you want to restore by hand Let the cloud tools finish syncing Erase the Mac If Erase All Content and Settings is unavailable After the wipe Back up and erase | mac.riera.co.uk Back up and erase a Mac Use this before selling or handing on a Mac, or when you want to start again from nothing. Back up the whole machine, check the backup, then erase it. Written for macOS 26 Tahoe on Apple silicon. 1 Make a fresh Time Machine backup Connect the backup disk or mount the network share. If it is not set up yet, add it in System Settings > General > Time Machine. Then start a backup and wait for it to finish: tmutil startbackup --block tmutil latestbackup tmutil needs Full Disk Access for your terminal app. If you have time, open the backup and spot-check the files you care about most. 2 Export what you want to restore by hand Time Machine covers everything, but these are easier to restore one at a time than to dig out of a backup: Keyboard Maestro macros and Karabiner-Elements rules A copy of the KeePassXC database Obsidian vaults, Logseq graphs and MailMate settings, wherever they live Dotfiles and SSH keys 3 Let the cloud tools finish syncing Check that Vivaldi Sync, VS Code Settings Sync and iCloud Drive have no uploads pending, and push any unpushed git work. 4 Erase the Mac Open System Settings > General > Transfer or Reset. Choose Erase All Content and Settings and enter your administrator password. Follow Erase Assistant. The Mac restarts, activates, and opens Setup Assistant. Erase Assistant signs you out of Apple services, turns off Find My and Activation Lock, removes the apps you installed, and deletes every user account and its data. If Erase All Content and Settings is unavailable Use macOS Recovery instead. Shut the Mac down, press and hold the power button until you see the startup options, and choose Options. Erase the disk in Disk Utility, then reinstall macOS. Keep the Mac online and plugged in while it reinstalls. After the wipe For a clean rebuild, set the Mac up as new and follow the from step 2. For a faster return, use Migration Assistant in Setup Assistant to bring accounts, apps and files back from the Time Machine backup. Keep the exports from step 2 either way. Restoring one app at a time is often cleaner than moving everything back. Commands come from , which also generates the Brewfiles. By

title: Rebuild a Mac | mac.riera.co.uk
summary: Step-by-step runbook for rebuilding a Mac on macOS 26 Tahoe with Apple silicon and Homebrew: back up, install, configure, restore, verify, then keep it updated.
body: Rebuild path Already set up Rebuild a Mac, from erased to working Back up first Go through Setup Assistant Install Homebrew and get the scripts Install the apps Set up the shell and terminal Apply macOS settings Tap to click Three-finger drag Dock Leave these off Set up the browser and coding tools Browser Coding tools Restore app state and licences Check the machine Already set up? Keep it updated Update everything See what changed since setup Check a bundle is complete After changing the repo Decisions and exclusions Rebuild a Mac | mac.riera.co.uk Jump to a step Rebuild path 1 Back up first 2 Setup Assistant 3 Homebrew and scripts 4 Install the apps 5 Shell and terminal 6 macOS settings 7 Browser and coding 8 Restore app state 9 Check the machine Already set up Rebuild a Mac, from erased to working The steps, commands and settings I use to turn a freshly erased Mac into my daily workstation. Work top to bottom, copy each command, and tick each step off as you go. Written for macOS 26 Tahoe on Apple silicon. App list last reviewed . Mac already set up? Go to . 1 Back up first Skip this on a brand-new Mac. On a Mac you are about to erase, make sure a recent Time Machine backup exists and points where you expect. tmutil latestbackup tmutil destinationinfo If either command says it is not permitted, give your terminal app Full Disk Access in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access. Homebrew cannot recreate these, so check they are in the backup or exported somewhere private: Keyboard Maestro macros and Karabiner-Elements rules Obsidian vaults and Logseq graphs MailMate accounts and rules Dotfiles, SSH keys and repo clones with unpushed work Leave out caches, node_modules , build output and anything you can download again. The full erase procedure is on . 2 Go through Setup Assistant Choose set up as new for a clean rebuild. Migration Assistant from Time Machine is faster, but it brings the old clutter back with it. Sign in with your Apple Account so iCloud, the App Store and Find My are ready. Turn on FileVault when asked. Apple Intelligence is offered during setup. You can change it later in System Settings > Apple Intelligence & Siri. Before installing anything else, install pending updates from System Settings > General > Software Update and restart. Homebrew then installs against the current system. 3 Install Homebrew and get the scripts The installer also installs Apple's Command Line Tools, which include git . It asks for your password. /bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)" Put brew on your PATH. The installer prints these lines when it finishes; on Apple silicon they are: echo 'eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"' >> ~/.zprofile eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)" brew doctor Then clone this repo. Later steps run its scripts from the repo folder. mkdir -p ~/Development git clone https://github.com/joanmarcriera/setup-a-mac-for-me.git ~/Development/setup-a-mac-for-me cd ~/Development/setup-a-mac-for-me 4 Install the apps Pick a bundle and run its commands. Workstation is the usual day-one install; Minimal and Full are smaller and larger versions of it. Expect the first run to take a while. Workstation bundle: the usual day-one rebuild for daily work. 53 formulae, 47 casks, 3 App Store apps. brew install bash wget vim uv tig htop tree tmux jq gh mas fzf ripgrep-all dust ncdu watch gping jdupes go volta mise pipx pandoc shellcheck git-cliff git-filter-repo git-lfs cmake hugo forgejo-cli colima docker docker-compose ollama llama.cpp whisper.cpp whisperkit-cli llmfit opencode herdr rtk qpdf poppler tesseract weasyprint pango ffmpeg yt-dlp gallery-dl gitleaks syft grype ykman brew install --cask iterm2 github google-chrome google-chrome@canary vivaldi comet duckduckgo visual-studio-code codex claude antigravity antigravity-cli lm-studio codexbar hive-app supacode t3-code meetily keyboard-maestro rectangle-pro karabiner-elements betterdisplay obsidian logseq mailmate@beta spotify slack discord telegram-desktop typora markedit zotero anki libreoffice drawio yed excalidrawz microsoft-edge microsoft-teams skim adobe-acrobat-reader shottr vlc blackhole-2ch blender bitwarden keepassxc # App Store: Microsoft Word, Microsoft Excel, Windows App mas install 462054704 462058435 1295203466 Turn on JavaScript to choose the Minimal or Full bundle here, or use the . Casks that install drivers, such as Karabiner-Elements and BlackHole, ask for your password and for approval in System Settings the first time they run. Every group, with its own command and notes, is in the . 5 Set up the shell and terminal Keep zsh plain and portable. Add these lines to ~/.zshrc . Homebrew's own line lives in ~/.zprofile from step 3, so it loads first. # Volta: Node.js versions export VOLTA_HOME="$HOME/.volta" export PATH="$VOLTA_HOME/bin:$PATH" # Rust, only if rustup is installed [ -f "$HOME/.cargo/env" ] && . "$HOME/.cargo/env" # mise: other runtimes. Activate after the PATH changes above. command -v mise >/dev/null && eval "$(mise activate zsh)" # ~/bin: personal scripts, including update-mac export PATH="$HOME/bin:$PATH" If you use Oh My Zsh, keep the plugin list to plugins=(git) . Do not add back autojump , zsh-syntax-highlighting or pnpm . In iTerm2, use a dark profile at about 20% transparency, and set Settings > Profiles > Keys > Key Mappings > Presets to Natural Text Editing so Option-arrow moves by word. 6 Apply macOS settings Tap to click System Settings > Trackpad > Point & Click > Tap to click, or run this and log out and back in: defaults write com.apple.AppleMultitouchTrackpad Clicking -bool true defaults write com.apple.driver.AppleBluetoothMultitouch.trackpad Clicking -bool true defaults -currentHost write NSGlobalDomain com.apple.mouse.tapBehavior -int 1 defaults write NSGlobalDomain com.apple.mouse.tapBehavior -int 1 Three-finger drag System Settings > Accessibility > Pointer Control > Trackpad Options. Turn on Use trackpad for dragging and set Dragging style to Three Finger Drag . Dock Show the hidden Dock without the delay. From the repo, ./scripts/apply-macos-defaults.sh applies the same settings. defaults write com.apple.dock autohide-time-modifier -float 0.5 defaults write com.apple.dock autohide-delay -int 0 killall Dock Leave these off App Exposé: System Settings > Trackpad > More Gestures > App Exposé. The Spotlight shortcut, if Keyboard Maestro needs Command-Space: System Settings > Keyboard > Keyboard Shortcuts > Spotlight. The old Launchpad grid tweak. macOS 26 replaced Launchpad with Apps in Spotlight, so springboard-columns and springboard-rows no longer change anything. 7 Set up the browser and coding tools Browser Make Vivaldi the default browser in System Settings > Desktop & Dock > Default web browser. In Vivaldi, set DuckDuckGo as the default search engine. Sign in to Vivaldi Sync and check that workspaces, bookmarks and extensions come back. Chrome, Chrome Canary and Edge are for compatibility testing, not daily browsing. Coding tools Sign in to VS Code and turn on Settings Sync. The Homebrew cask puts code on your PATH. Sign in to Codex, Claude and Antigravity. Containers run in colima with the plain docker CLI. Docker Desktop and OrbStack are not part of this setup. gh auth login colima start volta install node 8 Restore app state and licences This is the part most often forgotten. Open the password managers first so every other sign-in is quick. Open the KeePassXC database and sign in to Bitwarden. Keyboard Maestro: enter the licence, then import or sync macros and check the launcher and clipboard shortcuts. Rectangle Pro: enter the licence and restore the window shortcuts. Karabiner-Elements: restore the rules and approve its driver when macOS asks. BetterDisplay: restore presets for external monitors. Obsidian and Logseq: reopen the vaults and graphs. MailMate: restore accounts, IMAP settings and rules. Slack, Discord, Telegram and Teams: sign in. Word, Excel and Windows App: sign in with the Microsoft account. Ollama and LM Studio: download your local models again. They are large, so start early. Shottr: set the output folder and shortcuts. Keep licence keys in the password manager and app exports in a private backup, never in this repo. 9 Check the machine From the repo folder, pass the bundle you installed: minimal , workstation or all . The script lists any missing formula or cask and any Dock setting that does not match. ./scripts/verify-setup.sh workstation Turn Time Machine back on for this Mac in System Settings > General > Time Machine, then check by hand: Tap to click and three-finger drag work. Links open in Vivaldi, and searches go to DuckDuckGo. Keyboard Maestro shortcuts fire. docker run --rm hello-world prints its greeting. The first Time Machine backup has finished. Already set up? Keep it updated Three scripts in the repo: one updates everything, one shows what has drifted from the repo, and one checks a bundle is complete. Update everything Install the updater once: mkdir -p ~/bin cp ~/Development/setup-a-mac-for-me/scripts/update-mac.sh ~/bin/update-mac chmod +x ~/bin/update-mac Preview first, then run it: update-mac --dry-run update-mac It starts with a summary: macOS version, free disk space, the last Time Machine backup, and an upgrade plan that flags major version jumps, beta and canary channels, pinned formulae and macOS updates that need a restart. It changes nothing unless Time Machine has a backup from the last 7 days and the destination is reachable. Then it asks once per tool: Yes, No, Skip, All or Quit. It covers Homebrew, npm globals, App Store apps through mas , uv , pipx , Volta, rustup , mise and macOS updates, and prints install instructions for any tool that is missing. When a macOS update is pending, install it and restart first, then run update-mac again. --dry-run shows what every tool would do and changes nothing. It skips the Time Machine check. --yes runs without prompts. It does not stop for a pending macOS update. --greedy-casks also upgrades casks that update themselves. --skip-macos lists macOS updates but does not install them. --skip-backup-check skips the Time Machine check, for when your terminal lacks Full Disk Access. See what changed since setup Compares what is installed (Homebrew formulae, casks and App Store apps) with the repo. It lists what you added by hand, what is missing, and the commands to close each gap. It only reads; it changes nothing. ./scripts/drift-report.sh --bundle workstation compares against one bundle instead of every group. --ignore FILE skips tools you keep out of the repo on purpose. It reads ~/.config/mac-drift-ignore by default when that file exists. --json prints one JSON object for scripts. The exit status is 1 when it finds drift, so it works from cron or launchd. Check a bundle is complete Run ./scripts/verify-setup.sh workstation from the repo folder, as in . After changing the repo Edit data/install-groups.json , then regenerate the Brewfiles, the site data and the search index: python3 scripts/generate_brew_artifacts.py python3 scripts/build_search_index.py python3 scripts/check_docs.py Decisions and exclusions Why the list looks the way it does. Keyboard Maestro replaces Alfred, Raycast and separate clipboard managers. colima and the docker CLI replace Docker Desktop and OrbStack: free, scriptable, no licence. Volta manages Node.js and mise handles other runtimes. pnpm stays out. KeePassXC replaced KeeWeb, whose desktop releases stalled. MailMate stays on mailmate@beta because the stable cask needs Rosetta 2. Word, Excel and Windows App come from the App Store. Windows App replaces Microsoft Remote Desktop, whose cask is gone. OpenTofu is used instead of Terraform. App Exposé stays off. Everything dropped from the rebuild, with the reason, is listed at the end of the . Commands come from , which also generates the Brewfiles. By

title: Productivity
summary: Window management, keyboard automation, notes, and personal utilities.
body: keyboard-maestro rectangle-pro karabiner-elements betterdisplay obsidian logseq mailmate@beta spotify slack discord telegram-desktop Keyboard Maestro replaces Alfred, Raycast, and standalone clipboard managers. Keyboard Maestro and Rectangle Pro still require paid licenses after install. BetterDisplay stays because external monitor scaling and brightness control keep coming up. MailMate beta is the default on Apple Silicon because the stable cask currently requires Rosetta 2. Slack, Discord and Telegram stay in productivity because they are part of the day-to-day communications path. KeePassXC moved to the Security group.

title: PDF
summary: PDF readers and command-line PDF and OCR tooling.
body: qpdf poppler tesseract weasyprint pango skim adobe-acrobat-reader Skim is the fast lightweight reader. title: Network
summary: Diagnostics, remote access, and support tooling kept out of the default rebuild.
body: rclone mtr nmap tailscale-app netspot Useful when the Mac is doubling as a support or network box. The current Homebrew cask token is tailscale-app, not tailscale.
